saved.about:
Full runs, with the character development, relationships and team moments for Dick Grayson, Kory, Gar, Cyborg, Wally West and Raven. Books are in chronological eras, with major crossovers marked.

CORE = main reading path. IMPORTANT = meaningful character or continuity material.

blocks.text: The New Teen Titans (1984) #1–12 aren't skipped. The New Teen Titans (1984) was published alongside Tales of the Teen Titans, with its stories generally set ahead of the newsstand series. The two books eventually caught up with one another, which is why their issue numbers don't line up neatly.

For a straightforward reading path, finish Tales #57–58 and then read The New Teen Titans #1–49 as one continuous run. The Crisis placement is a broad crossover marker rather than a claim that the two series fit together issue by issue.

saved.title: X-Men
saved.about: Stay with Uncanny unless another series becomes genuinely relevant. When switching, read a decent chunk rather than jumping back and forth every issue. The big crossovers are where we use a tighter order.

blocks.text: 🔴 MUTANT MASSACRE

The first point to actually switch between books: the three main X-books are telling parts of the same event. You don't need the unrelated crossover tie-ins such as Thor, Daredevil or Power Pack for the X-Men story.
🔴 FALL OF THE MUTANTS
The three books tell separate stories during the same event, so there's no need to bounce between them issue by issue: read the three blocks.
🔴 INFERNO
The books become heavily interconnected again, so this uses the tighter order.
That gives you the context from all the X-books without turning the entire Claremont era into one giant issue-by-issue reading spreadsheet.
